A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same trie-based beam-search work and retain matching algorithms and core illustrations. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout, including v2 Appendices A and B. v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Phi-3.5-mini experiments on CNN/DailyMail, QMSUM and HumanEval, measuring generation quality, memory consumption and throughput in Table 1 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 reports original multi-model benchmark results, reasoning experiments, component ablations, fidelity checks and garbage-collection measurements, plus additional empirical results in both appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same shared-prefix KV cache, branch-specific masking, positional remapping and periodic garbage collection. v2's marking, pruning and compaction description elaborates the existing procedure; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: CNN/DailyMail summarization and HumanEval code generation remain, while QMSUM meeting summarization disappears. v2 adds MATH500 reasoning with chain-of-thought prompting and reports additional GSM8K and WMT evaluations in Appendix A, substantially revising task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds top-k sampling comparisons on MATH500 with k=3 and HumanEval with k=50 in Appendix B. Figure 3 also adds a greedy reference to the memory trajectories. Conventional batched beam search remains the principal comparator.

E3.justification: The Phi-only evaluation expands to Llama 3.1 8B and Mistral-Small 24B, with a limited 70B experiment in Appendix A and model-specific beam widths. Table 1 now states means over 1,000 samples instead of v1's dataset-specific counts, although sampling is unexplained. New protocols include logits checked until first divergence and garbage-collection timing over 1,000 decoding steps.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's memory-trajectory analysis, v2 adds trie-versus-garbage-collection ablations, per-token fidelity checks, garbage-collection overhead measurements, an indirect prefix-overlap analysis and a code-generation error case study. These address component contributions, behavioral fidelity and practical efficiency.

E5.justification: v1 gives an unspecified quality-significance statement with p>0.05. v2 names paired t-tests and McNemar tests, adds confidence intervals and significance markers for efficiency differences, and reports ablation uncertainty and dispersion across appendix settings. Confidence levels, interval construction and repeated-run details remain unspecified; Section 4.2 also inconsistently associates nonsignificance with p<0.01.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces benchmark values under revised reported settings and removes QMSUM results. For example, the Phi/HumanEval beam-15 trie accuracy is 0.6768 in v1 and newly reported as 0.70 in v2, without establishing a same-setting improvement. v2 also adds substantial numerical evidence in Tables 2–4, Figure 4 and the fidelity analysis.

T1.justification: The algorithmic mathematics and memory-efficiency formula remain unchanged. v2 adds explanations of masking, periodic rebuilding and computational scaling, but no new formal definition, theorem, proof or derivation. Its dense-attention qualification concerns the scope of the equivalence claim.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains memory-efficient beam search through shared-prefix caches. v2 explicitly qualifies theoretical equivalence by dense attention and changes the abstract's emphasis from preserving inference speed to quantified memory savings and faster decoding. These refine the retained contribution rather than introduce a new one.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability limits involving sparse attention, insufficient prefix overlap and garbage-collection slowdowns for small workloads. It also interprets the separate roles of trie sharing and garbage collection, and discusses reasoning accuracy, sequence length and efficiency tradeoffs. v1 largely emphasizes general applicability and low overhead.

D1.justification: v2 specifies garbage-collection stages and torch.index_select, reports a one-shot setting and clarifies GPU allocation by model. The printed repository owner changes from SpeedReach to brian030128, while v1's commit-specific HuggingFace baseline link disappears. These are documentation and access-information changes, without establishing a different decoding implementation.

R1.justification: The speculative-decoding discussion expands beyond SpecInfer to Medusa, staged speculative decoding and dynamic-width speculation, emphasizing global beam-search memory versus local sampling acceleration. v2 adds supporting references for sparse attention, nondeterminism, garbage collection and reasoning, while removing the earlier open-ended-generation discussion. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract and results narrative are substantially rewritten. v1's combined results-and-discussion section becomes separate fidelity and efficiency sections followed by a structured discussion, explicit limitations and appendices. Method explanations are expanded, and title, author and affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned into side-by-side model comparisons with differences, uncertainty and gain columns. Figure 3 changes its panel organization and visual encoding. v2 adds three tables, a garbage-collection timing plot and a code-comparison figure; the original method illustrations remain with shortened captions.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for generality and implementation efficiency: v1's single-model demonstration gains multiple attention configurations, component ablations, fidelity diagnostics, overhead measurements and explicit failure conditions. These address important gaps in the original validation. QMSUM coverage is lost, and reporting problems remain: Section 4.3 claims a 2.42× Phi speedup where Table 1 reports 2.10×, and the 1,000-sample description is unexplained. These weaknesses limit confidence in individual summaries but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in validation and scope qualification.
